newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close lower on export figures.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close lower on export figures.

text.p: A lower-than-expected number for soymeal in Thursday's USDA weekly export sales report pressured CBOT soy product futures to a lower close, traders said.
Traders were expecting a larger soymeal export number due to recent rumors of Chinese demand for U.S. and optional-origin soybeans and soymeal.
There were strong indications China last week bought beans and meal and there was talk early Wednesday China this week was seeking 300,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for October/November shipment.
There also was talk this week that China was seeking 450,000 tonnes of Oct/Nov U.S. and South American soymeal, the traders said.
But U.S. exporters Wednesday downplayed the China talk and said the tonnage being sought this week was small.
USDA's weekly report Thursday revealed China, in the week ended October 3 purchased 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal.
Soyoil closed 0.15 to 0.28 cent per lb lower, with October down 0.25 at 23.30. Soymeal was $0.10 to $4.50 per ton lower, with October down $0.10 at $248.70.
